                                                                       III
    PREFACE
To boost the numerous effort by Mathematicians in addressing the perennial problems
of poor understanding and its attendant low grades in the subject, this book covers the
NEW SSCE syllabus directly including oversight areas.
A pool of past questions over the years on each topics were painstakingly collected ;
part of which were used as an additional examples to illustrate elaborately the required
concepts on each topics while similar ones were left as exercises.
Answers and mathematical tables are provided at the end of the text.

         Approximation                                                        Solution

   Decimal and Significant figures                            In significant figures, our concern is the first figure, not zero
                                                              or decimal point. So we take 247 for 3s.f and approximate
These twin concepts are working tools for presenting
most answers in mathematics. The author deliberately                  0.002473  0.00247 ( C )
fixed them together to avoid the usual confusion              We round down by adding nothing 247
associated with them. Once the next digit to the one          Since after 247 in 0.002473 we have 3 which is below 5
being considered is any of 5, 6, 7, 8, 9; we round up i.e.
adding 1 to our digit.                                        2005/3 (Nov)
On the other hand, if the digit is any of 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 we
round down, i.e adding nothing to our digit.                  Which of these numbers is correct to three significant figures?
Examples.

Change of subject of the Formula                                 2005/ 2a
The term change of subject of the formula implies
transformation of a given formula to make another                ( i ) Make t the subject of relation k = m         t -3
quantity (usually a letter) the subject of the equation.                                                            t -9
This is other than the one in that position.
In doing it, basic mathematical rules must not be                ( ii ) Find the value of t, if k = 2 and m = 1
violated.                                                                           Solution

Some Basic Guides                                                          k= m                t -3
                                                                                               t -9
(a) Remove square or square root if present
(b) Clear fractions, clear bracket if they exist                 Since T is under square root, we take square of both sides
(c) Collect like terms together involving the required subject.
(d) If necessary factorize the term on each side of                      k2     =     m2    t  -  3  
                                                                                            t  -  9
   the equation
(e) Isolate the required subject usually by division                       k2 =    m2t - 3m2
                                                                                      t -9
   by a common factor
                                                                 Cross multiply to clear fraction
Note                                                                 k2(t ­ 9) = m2t ­ 3m2
                                                                 Collect terms in t together
The above stated guides are no strict rules to be                    k2t ­ m2t = 9k2 ­ 3m2
followed when solving any problem under this topic;                  t(k2 ­ m2) = 9k2 ­ 3m2
rather, they are guides which readers will find useful

Cases involving indices(powers)                                              t=       9k 2 - 3m2

form to reduce the stress and space of writing very large    C 5.02  10 ­ 4 D 5.02  10 ­ 3
or very small numbers.

Median (frequency distribution)                            (a) Median working

To get median for frequency data, we apply the idea of          f is 2 + 5 +13 +11 + 9 +10 i.e 50 which is even
odd and even numbers to get the median class or
column among other columns or classes. f is another             Median class =  f
important term for us to know, which is " Summation
of frequency". The two ways of getting our median                                        2
class or column are:
                                                                                = 50 i.e 25th class
(a) Median class (column) = f if f is even
                                     2                                                   2

(b) Median class (column) = f + 1 if f is odd              Adding frequency cumulatively till we get to 25th class:
                                      2                                 2 + 5 +13 +11 i.e 4th column,
                                                                        Thus, median = 4

adding the frequency of the given data till we get to the  2007/12a NABTEB

BEARING                                                   Acute ­ angled Triangle

This topic deals with measurement of points on the                            A
earth surface based on some principles of which part
has been discussed. The resulting shapes are mostly              c               b

Discrete data & continuous data                                      SD = 699837.34
Discrete data have distinct values without intermediate
points. The number of student(s) in a class could be                                 50
0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5,... but not 1.5 or 25.6 or 50.1
impossible ! Frequency can also be attached such as:                     = 13996.7468 = 118.3078  118.31 to 2d.p
the number of girls, number of boys and number of
absentees in a class.                                           2007/13 Adjusted Exercise 17.1
Where as if we are to consider the weight of students in        In a college, the number of absentees recorded over a period
a class; values such as 16kg, 16.4kg, 17.1kg, 19.3kg
20.0kg etc. the result will be both whole and fractional        of 30 days was as shown in the frequency distribution table
or intermediate values. This will require a range say
16­20. Hence continuous data have values over a                 Number of 0 ­ 4      5­9  10 ­ 14 15­ 19 20 ­ 24
range of whole number or fraction.                              absentees

Note that when a continuous data is treated as fixed, it        Number of 1          5    10         9            5

becomes discrete                                                     days

    Plane mensuration
 Area & perimeter of plane shapes                             Factorizing 36; 2  18, 2  2  9 i.e 4 and 9
Area and perimeter are terms used in mensuration.             x2 + 9x ­ 4x ­ 36 = 0
Students tend to confuse the two terms thus,                  x(x + 9) ­ 4(x + 9) = 0
interchanging the formulae to be used.
To give a clear difference between them, let us consider            (x + 9)(x ­ 4) = 0
an example of a football field that is rectangular in shape.                  x + 9 = 0 or x ­ 4 = 0
The 11 players of both teams play within the pitch area                           x = ­ 9 or 4
and the referee officiates within the pitch (area)
                                                              We accept x = 4cm as width
                       Players and referee
                                                              (ii) Perimeter = 2(L + b)
As for the assistant referee (lines' men ) they work                          = 2 [(x + 5) + x]
within the lines outside the field (perimeter). They run
round the length and breadth of the field but not within               = 2 [(4 + 5) + 4]
the field as the players
                                                                       = 2 (13)
                 Assistant referee (line's men)                        = 26cm

            logic                                              The words and, or, not,... then, and if and only if are
The basic problem of logic is the analysis of the              the basic words used to connect propositions. They are
methods of reasoning. Reasoning is that special kind of        called logical connectives
thinking called inference, in which conclusions are
drawn from premises. As an example consider:                   Use of Symbols

All dogs have four legs.                                       The power of symbolic Logic lies in its use of
Bingo is a dog
Therefore, Bingo has four legs.                                symbols to represent proposition and connectives. We shall
The premises of this argument are all dogs have four
legs and bingo is a dog. The conclusion is Bingo has           represent propositions by the lower case letters p, q, r,...
four legs.                                                     usually, each letter will stand for a simple proposition and

The logician seeks the answer to this question. "If the        compound will be formed by linking two or more letters
premises are true, is one justified in saying that the
conclusion is true?". If so, the reasoning that led to the     together by means of one or more of logical connectives and
conclusion is valid (logical); if not, the reasoning is
invalid (illogical). The systematic formalization and          also give the name by which the compound is known
cataloging of valid methods of reasoning is one of the
major task of a logician. If his work uses abstract            Connectives Symbol Names of compound
symbols, then it is called symbolic logic.

Definitions
A matrix with m rows and n columns is called an
m by n matrix. Where m × n or m by n is called the
size or shape of the matrix.
